selected_evidence.requirement: node1 configured to route between lan-a (node2) and lan-b (node3) with original source addresses preserved
selected_evidence.summary: VyOS interfaces eth1/eth2 configured and committed; node2 pings node3 across the router; tcpdump on node1's lan-b interface shows the TCP SYN from node2 arriving with unmodified source 10.10.1.10 (no NAT), proving direct reachability with preserved source addresses.
Arbitrary TCP port (5001/5002) nc session from node2 to node3 succeeded and delivered payload, showing forwarding works for arbitrary ports, not just a hardcoded rule.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart persistence (boot identity change + recovery)
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id ebd78841...; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id 428d4ad0... confirms restart; VyOS config.boot shows persisted eth1/eth2 addresses and forwarding still enabled; ping node2->node3 succeeds post-reboot.

selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id a8b262d7...; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id cbcb28f7... confirms restart; /etc/network/interfaces persisted the eth1 static IP and route hook, ping to node3 succeeds post-reboot.
